It opens with Halloween landing on a Saturday, which has pushed almost every good party indoors and spread the rest across both Friday and Saturday night. Then comes the real centre of the edition: November 2, when the Mission builds several hundred altars in a park and walks 24th Street by candlelight, and Oakland closes nine blocks of Fruitvale the day before. There are seven separate Day of the Dead observances here across four counties, and six of the seven are free. After that the window turns athletic. The Warriors come home 0-3 for the longest homestand of their season, nine Chase Center dates in all. The Earthquakes play two final home matches with playoff seeding still live, and Bay FC says goodbye to a hard year on November 1. Then the holiday machinery starts: a coffee festival, a tea festival, a chocolate salon, Dickens Fair, Lightscape, and four turkey trots in four counties on Thanksgiving morning. One thing needs deciding this week rather than later. Dickens Fair's Early Bird pricing, which covers the opening weekends and saves ten dollars a head, is only on sale through October 31. Pick of the Month Day of the Dead in the Mission Festival of Altars and the Ritual Procession, Monday November 2 Two events, one evening, and they are designed to be done together. From ten in the morning the community builds altars in Potrero del Sol Park, with a ceremony at sunset and a performance at eight. At seven the procession gathers at Bryant and 22nd and walks toward 24th Street with drums, Aztec dancers and several thousand people moving mostly in silence. Food vendors line the procession route rather than the park. Both are free. Why this one Most of what fills a five-week calendar can be caught again next year, or next month, or in another city. This cannot. The Marigold Project has run the Festival of Altars for more than three decades and it only works on November 2, only in that neighbourhood, and only because a few thousand people show up and build it themselves. It costs nothing, it asks something of you, and it is the single most San Francisco thing happening between now and December. Bring a photograph of someone you have lost. Warren Hellman died in 2011. The festival has not charged a cent since, and roughly 750,000 people turn up across the three days. The 2026 bill has now had three announcement rounds. Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, My Morning Jacket, Alison Krauss, Sierra Hull, Old Crow Medicine Show, Hiss Golden Messenger, Kathleen Edwards, Yasmin Williams with William Tyler, AJ Lee and Blue Summit, El Khat and Tyler Ballgame are all confirmed, with more still to come. What tips it from very good to unmissable this year is the night before. On Thursday October 1 the Masonic hosts An Evening Honoring Steve Earle, with Emmylou Harris, Jackson Browne, Hot Tuna, Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, Molly Tuttle, Buddy Miller, Larry Campbell and Teresa Williams and others, benefiting Sweetwater Spectrum. That lineup will not assemble again. Practical advice: do not drive. The N Judah, the 5 Fulton and the 7 all serve the park and all of them will be full. Go in on foot from the east end, bring a layer for when the fog comes in around four, and wear boots if there has been rain, because Hellman Hollow turns to mud faster than you would think.
